Here is a modified fiddle: http://jsfiddle.net/jjhh6zh8/12/

Not quite sure what is going on...

I have the same thing in version 69, but only when I try to cast a shadow with a directional light. I have this scene using a spotlight with no errors: 
http://analogmadness.com/Demo/ThreeJS/spinningBox.html
While this scene using a directional light does give out the errors:
http://analogmadness.com/Demo/ThreeJS/index.html
@Dinkelborg Would you be willing to provide a simple, 50-line example that demonstrates your issue?

Well I sure would, but I don't know what causes it. 
I am receiving the message: [.WebGLRenderingContext]GL ERROR :GL_INVALID_OPERATION : glDrawElements: range out of bounds for buffer

Since the directionalLight was not casting any shadows I thought it would be that, but when I only put a cube a ground and a directionalLight in a scene the error does not show it must be somewhere in here:
http://bit.ly/1xgfz6P
I tried to reduce it to a 50 line issue but as mentioned, it was gone...
Besides that I can also say that in Firefox the error message is another namely:
"THREE.WebGLProgram: gl.getProgramInfoLog()" "(60,2-97): warning X3557: loop only executes for 1 iteration(s), forcing loop to unroll
(80,2-97): warning X3557: loop only executes for 1 iteration(s), forcing loop to unroll

" three.js:24586
"THREE.WebGLProgram: gl.getProgramInfoLog()" "(71,2-97): warning X3557: loop only executes for 1 iteration(s), forcing loop to unroll

" three.js:24586
@Dinkelborg Sorry, we can't debug your application. If you are able to produce a simple jsfiddle to demonstrate a problem, that would be very much appreciated.
@WestLangley Was there any resolution or workaround to this problem?: http://jsfiddle.net/mdeem/jjhh6zh8/

@manthrax No, sorry. Do you agree that http://jsfiddle.net/jjhh6zh8/13/ is also a demonstration of your issue? ( r.69)

EDIT: updated fiddle

Ah thanks for getting back @WestLangley... yeah that looks like the same issue.

I'm guessing that frustum culling causes some buffer regeneration to be deferred until later, but the meshes are still trying to be rendered before their buffers have been generated. I have the same issue in my app, but it resolves itself after a number of frames, so I'm not sweating it for now...

Found this because I had also warnings after integrating shadows into my project. Can't pinpoint it either except it's related to some objects casting shadows not being drawn.

Manthrax' "fix" works for me as well.

I experience the exact same thing. With both BasicShadowMapand PCFSoftShadowMap I get "[.WebGLRenderingContext]GL ERROR :GL_INVALID_OPERATION : glDrawElements: range out of bounds for buffer". No errors without shadows enabled.

The shadows seem to work ok (though I get an occasional flicker in 69 that I didn't see in 68).
The problem is that `WebGLRenderer` is not doing `updateObject( object )` because is not visible from the main camera. Micro-optimisations...
Fixed! (Slowly getting `WebGLRenderer` more and more under control...! ^^)
